original_title: AQbD-Driven RP-HPLC Method for Rapid Dissolution Monitoring of Amiodarone Hydrochloride Tablets Without Sample Dilution
title: Skipping the 10x dilution step in amiodarone dissolution testing
blurb: The compendial USP method for amiodarone HCl tablets needs a 10-fold dilution just to keep polysorbate 80 from wrecking the column, and direct injection normally trashes peak shape. This AQbD-designed RP-HPLC method gets around that and injects straight, worth a look if it holds up as a QC replacement.

original_title: Florida Theranostics: Advanced Imaging & Precision Radioligand Therapies with Dr. Ashok Muthu Krishn - WFLX
title: A Florida theranostics shop talks up its imaging and radioligand therapy lineup
blurb: A local TV segment with Dr. Ashok Muthu Krishn covering Florida Theranostics' imaging and radioligand therapy offerings. Promotional, not data, so read it as a signal of where clinics are investing rather than a result.

original_title: 3D-Printed Stackable Air–Liquid Interface Platform for Isotopic Tracing of Cancer-Derived Volatiles
title: Stacking cell cultures to actually catch the volatiles they breathe out
blurb: Standard in vitro setups leak too few volatile organic compounds to profile well. This 3D-printed, paper-based air-liquid interface stacks multiple lung cancer cell culture layers into one shared headspace, using low-emissive materials so the platform itself doesn't add noise, aimed at getting isotopic tracing of cancer-derived volatiles to actually work at trace levels.

original_title: Solution Phase Protein Dynamics: Influences of ESI Buffers on Hydration
title: The ESI buffer you pick is quietly changing the protein you're measuring
blurb: Comparing ammonium acetate, EDDA, and TEAA by native mass spec on transthyretin, wild-type and four disease mutants, shows these supposedly neutral ESI buffers aren't bystanders, they measurably reshape hydration, dynamics, and stability. Worth knowing before treating buffer choice as inert in native MS work.

original_title: So how is AI drug discovery doing, really?
title: So how is AI drug discovery doing, really?
blurb: Another great column from Derek Lowe. I won't spoil you the pleasure of reading through it, but will just post this quote, which I find beautifully spot-on. “Although a wide variety of AI methods have been developed, applied and benchmarked, evidence of their clinically relevant impact is, so far, disappointingly limited. . .It can be concluded that we are still at a stage with an ‘absence of evidence’ (and not necessarily an ‘evidence of absence’) when it comes to the translation of AI into clinically relevant impact.”

original_title: Site-Specific Native Antibody-Conjugated Microbubbles for Molecular Ultrasound Imaging of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
title: Ultrasound microbubbles get a click-chemistry antibody handle
blurb: LASIC conjugation puts anti-GPC3 antibodies on microbubbles through a DBCO click adapter at the antibody's heavy chain, instead of the usual random lysine coupling that can quietly wreck antigen binding. Blocking experiments confirm the specificity holds, aimed at picking out GPC3-positive liver cancer by ultrasound rather than MRI or PET.

original_title: Structure-resolved virus-host interactomics by cross-linking mass spectrometry.
title: Mapping virus-host contacts with a crosslinker and a mass spec
blurb: A review on using cross-linking mass spectrometry to resolve virus-host protein interactions at structural resolution, not just which proteins touch but how they're arranged when they do. It's a survey piece, so no new data here, just the state of the toolkit.

original_title: Improved Identification of Peptides, Modification Sites, and Cross-Link Sites by Target-Enhanced Accurate Inclusion Mass Screening (TAIMS).
title: TAIMS squeezes more crosslink IDs out of the same run
blurb: Target-enhanced accurate inclusion mass screening steers the instrument toward masses it already expects to matter, and comes out with better identification of peptides, modification sites, and cross-link sites for it.

original_title: Payload-Free [89Zr]Zr-DFO*-sq-Enfortumab ImmunoPET for Imaging Nectin-4 Expression in Bladder Cancer
title: Enfortumab without the payload, just for imaging
blurb: Enfortumab is normally an ADC, payload included, but strip that off and radiolabel the naked antibody with Zr-89 via a DFO*-sq chelator and you get an immunoPET tracer for Nectin-4 in bladder cancer. The point is dodging the pharmacologic confounding that payload-bearing ADC tracers introduce, along with the renal clearance and urinary background problems that dogged earlier Nectin-4 tracers.

original_title: Non-specific cysteine modifications on proteins induced by trans-cyclooctene.
title: Your bioorthogonal handle might be tagging cysteines you didn't ask for
blurb: Trans-cyclooctene, the click handle everyone reaches for in tetrazine ligation, turns out to modify cysteines on proteins non-specifically. Worth knowing if you've been treating TCO tags as inert bystanders in your labeling scheme.

original_title: Radiolabelled somatostatin receptor antagonist versus agonist for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy in patients with metastatic pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma: a retrospective pilot study
title: Antagonist PRRT out-doses the agonist, in the same patients
blurb: A retrospective pilot comparing Lu-177-DOTA-JR11 (antagonist) against Lu-177-DOTA-TOC (agonist) dosimetry within the same metastatic pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma patients who'd already run out of conventional options. The antagonist delivers higher tumor and organ absorbed dose, matching what antagonist PRRT has claimed elsewhere, but it's a small retrospective look at a rare disease, so pilot data only.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Effect of Functional Groups Introduced into Radioiodinated Asymmetric Cyanine Dyes on Their In Vivo Behavior
title: The 'spare' side chain on cyanine dyes isn't actually spare
blurb: Asymmetric heptamethine cyanine dyes use one indole side to bind albumin and ride the EPR effect into tumors, leaving the other side free for conjugating a drug. This radioiodinated series shows the functional groups hung on that supposedly free side still shift the dye's in vivo behavior, so it's not neutral real estate for whatever payload you bolt on.

original_title: A low-crosslinking hydrogel integrating prodrug nanoparticles modulates neuroinflammation and ECM deposition for enhanced spinal cord regeneration.
title: A softer hydrogel packed with prodrug nanoparticles for spinal cord repair
blurb: A low-crosslinking hydrogel carrying prodrug nanoparticles, built to calm neuroinflammation and reshape ECM deposition after spinal cord injury to help regeneration along.

original_title: Chemoenzymatic Radiosynthesis of a Gluconate Transporter‐Targeted In Vivo Bacterial Sensor From Clinical [ 18 F]FDG
title: Turning FDG into a bacteria-only PET tracer with one enzyme
blurb: Bacteria can import and metabolize gluconate through GntP and GntK, mammalian cells can't, so [18F]FGA targets exactly that gap for pathogen-specific PET. The synthesis is just glucose oxidase acting on clinical [18F]FDG that's already sitting on the shelf, and it picked up broad detection sensitivity across multiple bacterial species.

original_title: Stereospecific Peptide–Polysaccharide Conjugates Enable Noninvasive Therapy of Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
title: Chirality decides whether this eye conjugate actually works
blurb: Stereospecific peptide-polysaccharide conjugates were built in both L- and D- forms, and only the D-PPC showed real chirality-dependent bioactivity with high-affinity target binding. The payoff being chased is treating neovascular AMD without the repeated intravitreal injections that make posterior-segment eye disease such a pain to dose.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Total Synthesis of D -Fuc p 3NAc Containing Conjugation-Ready Pentasaccharide Repeating Unit Related to Acinetobacter baumannii RCH51
title: First total synthesis of a superbug's five-sugar capsule
blurb: A convergent (4+1) block glycosylation nails three consecutive 1,2-cis linkages plus the rare sugar ddD-Fucp3NAc, the fiddly bit made on gram scale from glucose. It comes out linker-appended and conjugation-ready, so this reads like a vaccine precursor, not just a synthesis flex.

original_title: Total Synthesis of ent ‐Kaurenoic Acid Diterpenoids Enabled by Distal Conformational Control in Photoredox Radical Polyene Cyclization
title: Light-driven polyene cyclization builds the kaurenoic acid cage
blurb: A photoredox radical polyene cyclization where a chiral bicyclo[3.2.1]octane unit steers stereochemistry from a distance, assembling the full 6/6/6/5 ent-kaurenoic acid framework under visible light. A nickel-catalyzed reductive coupling builds the cyclization substrate first, so it's a two-stage strategy dressed up as one paper.

original_title: Phosphine-mediated azine C–H couplings with water and ammonia
title: Azine C–H bonds coupled straight to water and ammonia
blurb: A phosphine-mediated method that installs OH or NH2 onto azine C–H bonds directly, using water or ammonia as the nitrogen and oxygen source instead of a pre-installed leaving group.

original_title: Bioactive Spermidine-Crosslinked DNA Hydrogel for rapid homeostasis and accelerated wound healing
title: A DNA hydrogel that clots like a NET instead of gluing to the wound
blurb: Crosslinked with spermidine rather than an inert linker, so the gel itself carries autophagy-inducing, cardioprotective, anti-inflammatory activity while structurally mimicking neutrophil extracellular traps. The actual pitch is that most hemostats stop bleeding fine but tear the wound open again on removal, and this one's built not to.

original_title: Conformationally Dictated Divergent Triplet Reactivity of Conjugated Dienes: Visible-Light-Induced Electrocyclization, 1,5-HAT, and Cycloaddition
title: One diene, three photochemical fates depending on how it's allowed to twist
blurb: Energy-transfer photocatalysis pushes conjugated dienes toward electrocyclization, 1,5-HAT, or cycloaddition, and which one wins comes down to whether the cyclic backbone can tolerate the twisted trans-cycloalkene intermediate needed to get there. Same substrate class, three outcomes, sorted by ring strain rather than by swapping catalysts.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Increased number of crosslinking sites for factor XIII counteracts the mechanical and lytic destabilization of fibrin caused by citrullination of fibrinogen.
title: Extra factor XIII crosslinks patch up citrullinated fibrin clots
blurb: Citrullinating fibrinogen makes the resulting fibrin clot mechanically weaker and easier to break down, and increasing the number of factor XIII crosslinking sites counteracts both effects. Not much more detail to go on than that.

original_title: Regioselective Nucleophilic Diamination of Quinones Enabling Access to 3,5-, 3,6-, and Mixed Diamino Derivatives: Synthesis and Photocurrent Characterization
title: Quinone diamination goes 3,5 or 3,6 depending which amine you grab
blurb: A Cu(OTf)2 catalyst run under air gives 3,6-diaminoquinones from anilines, a mix of 3,6/3,5 from primary aliphatic amines, and clean 3,5-isomers from bulky secondary amines, regiochemistry set by sterics and catalyst coordination rather than by changing conditions. They also checked the products' photocurrent response, so it's not purely a methods paper.

original_title: Divergent Synthesis of Hydropyrimidines and Imidazolines Via Hypervalent Iodine-Mediated Dearomatization
title: Same hypervalent iodine intermediate, two dearomatization products, your choice of acid
blurb: Swap the acid counterion on a hypervalent iodine system and a pyrimidine dearomatization forks: triflic acid contracts the ring to imidazolines, hydrogen halides trap the intermediate and keep the ring intact as halogenated hydropyrimidines. DFT pins down the actual branch point, a nice touch for a paper that's mostly about which acid bottle you reach for.

original_title: A Synthetic β‐Mannan Epitope Enables Immunization and Detection of Candida auris
title: One synthetic sugar tag both vaccinates against and detects Candida auris
blurb: A synthetic β-mannan tetrasaccharide epitope, conjugated to CRM197, raised epitope-selective IgM and IgG and cut fungal burden in kidneys, against a multidrug-resistant fungus that currently has neither a vaccine nor a fast diagnostic. The same glycan doing double duty as immunogen and detection reagent is the actual hook.

original_title: Antibody-drug conjugates: Why it takes a village to make them - Chemical & Engineering News
title: Making an ADC takes a whole supply chain, not one chemist
blurb: A look at how many separate specialists, antibody producers, linker and payload suppliers, CDMOs, actually have to line up before one antibody-drug conjugate reaches manufacturing.

original_title: Reaction of Thioesters and Selenoesters with Diazo Reagents: Formal Carbene Insertion into C–S and C–Se Bonds
title: Carbenes learn to insert themselves into C–S and C–Se bonds
blurb: Rh- or Cu-generated carbenes from diazo reagents slide into the C(O)–S and C(O)–Se bonds of thioesters and selenoesters, formal insertion demonstrated across 37 examples. They isolated a key intermediate and ran DFT to pin down the mechanism, and the payoff is products stacked with up to four different activating groups on one carbon.

original_title: Electrocatalytic Ethanol‐to‐Acetate Conversion With Nearly 100% Faradaic Efficiency Enabled by Cu‐Doping Strategy for Enhancing Selective and Cooperative Adsorption
title: Cu-doping fixes nickel's ethanol oxidation problem
blurb: Ni(OH)2 catalysts for turning ethanol into acetate, paired with hydrogen production at the other electrode, usually suffer because ethanol and OH- compete badly for adsorption sites. Doping in copper balances that out, and the result is near 100% Faradaic efficiency holding for 108 hours, with in situ electrochemistry and calculations backing the adsorption story.

original_title: Divergent Synthesis of Ketones and Alcohols via Iron-Catalyzed Three-Component Alcohol Cross-Coupling
title: One iron catalyst, same alcohols, ketone or alcohol depending on how you steer it
blurb: A borrowing-hydrogen cross-coupling that takes three different alcohols and routes them to either a ketone or an alcohol product from the same starting materials and catalyst. The real trick is selective cross-coupling of three alcohol components instead of the usual two, which is exactly where earlier systems tended to make a mess.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Direct Deaminative Borylation of Anilines – A Retro-Chan–Evans–Lam Reaction
title: Turning anilines directly into arylboronates, no diazonium salt required
blurb: A copper-catalyzed deaminative borylation that runs the Chan-Evans-Lam reaction backwards: anomeric amide activation kicks off aryl radicals from isodiazene intermediates, which get intercepted by a Cu-Bpin species. The N-fluorosulfonamide oxidant is doing real work, keeping the copper cycling while generating the electrophilic radical needed for a polarity-matched HAT step.

original_title: BN-Sequence Extension of Heterophenalene Analogs via the Sugasawa-type Double Annulation: Single-Atom Sequence Perturbation Controls Molecular Binding in Isoelectronic Scaffolds of BN-Embedded Aromatics
title: Swapping one boron or nitrogen in a BN-aromatic changes how it binds
blurb: Using the Sugasawa reaction to build an NBN pattern off boron diaminonaphthalene, extending the BN sequence along two zigzag directions and embedding a BN3 unit as a binding site, with the same approach working for an NCN-patterned analog too. The point: even a single-atom change in the boron/nitrogen sequence measurably shifts sp2/sp3 interconversion at the boron center on binding, a rare model system for metal-free catalysis.

original_title: Radical 1,3-Difunctionalization of β,γ-Unsaturated Ketones via Synergistic LMCT and RLT Photocatalysis
title: An iron photocatalyst that moves the carbonyl to make room for 1,3-diazidation
blurb: Combines 1,2-functional group migration with LMCT and radical ligand transfer under iron photocatalysis, and the payoff is the first 1,3-diazidation and 1,3-dichlorination of β,γ-unsaturated ketones, routed through a 1,2-carbonyl migration. Broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, per the authors.

original_title: Sonesitatug vedotin demonstrated a statistically significant and highly clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival in 2nd and later-line CLDN18.2-positive advanced gastric/GEJ cancers - AstraZeneca
title: AstraZeneca's CLDN18.2 ADC posts an actual survival win in gastric cancer
blurb: Sonesitatug vedotin, AstraZeneca's CLDN18.2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate, hit a statistically significant and clinically meaningful overall survival improvement in second-line-and-later CLDN18.2-positive advanced gastric/GEJ cancer. No numbers yet and it's the company's own readout, but clearing a survival endpoint in later-line gastric cancer is nothing to sneeze at.

original_title: Energy-Transfer-Driven [2 + 2] Cycloaddition: Synthesis of Cyclobutane-Fused Tetracycles from Indenes and Maleimides
title: Visible light welds indenes and maleimides into cyclobutane-fused tetracycles
blurb: A photocatalytic [2+2] between indenes and maleimides running through energy transfer: the excited photosensitizer activates the maleimide first, then cyclization builds the fused tetracyclic cyclobutane skeleton. The draw is Fsp3 and conformational rigidity, delivered in one step instead of stepwise.

original_title: Ti(III)-Mediated Selective α–α′ Homocoupling of Allylic Epoxides: A Direct Route to Symmetrical Homoallylic 1,4-Diols
title: Titanocene(III) opens allylic epoxides the other way, straight to symmetrical 1,4-diols
blurb: Cp2TiCl2/Mn radical opening of allylic epoxides is usually γ-selective through allyltitanium intermediates, but minimally substituted epoxides here flip to highly selective α-α' homocoupling instead, giving symmetrical homoallylic 1,4-diols with no γ-γ' or γ-α' byproducts detected. Substrates carrying a pendant alkene even skip cyclization, which is the tell that the regioselectivity is substitution-driven rather than incidental.

original_title: Direct Synthesis of Pyrazolones via N–B Bond Functionalization: Sequential Carbonyl Insertion Using In Situ Generated N , N ′-Diborylated Hydrazines
title: Metal-free route to pyrazolones runs through a diborylated hydrazine intermediate
blurb: A 4,4'-bipyridyl-catalyzed protocol generates N,N'-diborylated hydrazines in situ from azoarenes and B2pin2, then inserts carbonyls from β-keto esters sequentially to build 1,2-diaryl pyrazol-3-ones, no metal catalyst needed. Scales to grams, and the products show promising anti-inflammatory activity, more than most methodology papers bother to check.

original_title: Comparative assessment of KDIGO and CTCAE criteria for detecting renal function deterioration after peptide receptor radionuclide therapy
title: CTCAE or KDIGO: which one actually catches PRRT kidney damage
blurb: 149 GEP-NET patients on peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, followed for at least a year, used to see whether oncology's usual CTCAE eGFR grading or nephrology's KDIGO staging better flags real renal deterioration and predicts where kidney function ends up long term. Telling that oncology and nephrology haven't even agreed on how to grade a kidney.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Analytical Quality By Design-Based Development And Validation Of A Stability-Indicating RP-HPLC Method For Simultaneous Determination Of Triamcinolone Acetonide And Econazole Nitrate In Pharmaceutical Cream Formulation
title: One HPLC run for both drugs in an antifungal steroid cream
blurb: A stability-indicating RP-HPLC method for simultaneously quantifying triamcinolone acetonide and econazole nitrate in cream formulations, tuned via a proper three-factor, five-level Central Composite Design rather than the usual one-variable-at-a-time fumbling. QC infrastructure, not a discovery, but a solidly built one.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Generalising metallaphotoredox alkyl and aryl methylation with photoactive quinoline-based organoaluminium
title: An aluminum photocatalyst that methylates almost anything
blurb: A quinoline-ligated aluminum complex forms in situ and drives metallaphotoredox methylation across carboxylic acids, alcohols, amines, halides and arenes, one catalyst instead of a different recipe for each coupling partner. The trick is a hydroxylated diarylquinoline that acts as a non-innocent ligand, doing real electronic work instead of just sitting on the metal. Earth-abundant metal doing a job usually reserved for iridium or ruthenium.

original_title: Germyl Radical Cyclization of Enynes and Dienes under Visible-Light Irradiation
title: Building germanium rings with light instead of tin reagents
blurb: Visible-light photoredox paired with HAT catalysis turns 1,6-enynes and dienes into germanium-containing heterocycles through a radical hydrogermylation/cyclization cascade, mild conditions, broad substrate scope, five-membered carbagermanes as the headline product. Germanium radical chemistry doesn't get this kind of toolkit often.

original_title: Method Development and Validation of Capmatinib in Solid Dosage Form by RP-HPLC Method
title: Another QC method, this time for capmatinib tablets
blurb: A validated RP-HPLC assay for capmatinib in bulk drug and marketed tablets, C18 column, methanol and dilute orthophosphoric acid running 70:30. Nothing exotic, just the kind of method a QC lab needs on file before it can release batches.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: BWXT Selling Medical Business to Nordic Capital in Transaction Valued at up to $800 Million - The Globe and Mail
title: BWXT sells off its medical business for up to $800M
blurb: Nordic Capital is buying BWXT's medical unit in a deal valued up to $800 million. Nice payday for BWXT; whether isotope supply priorities survive a private-equity handoff is the part worth actually watching.

original_title: Cycloaddition-Based Retrosynthetic Logic for the Diversification and Molecular Editing of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
title: Editing PAHs by snapping rings on and off instead of building from scratch
blurb: A cycloaddition/cycloreversion-based retrosynthetic strategy for diversifying and molecularly editing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, sidestepping the usual multistep routes that need prefunctionalized arenes and strong oxidants. Fewer steps to reroute a PAH core is the actual selling point.

original_title: Cross-Metathesis of an Iron Carbene with Diazenes
title: Getting olefin metathesis to finally touch a diazene
blurb: Iron carbene complexes reacting with cyclic diazenes to pull off a cross-metathesis that's eluded olefin catalysts until now, diazene/olefin metathesis stayed unrealized because nobody had worked out how nitrogen-rich substrates deactivate the usual catalysts. Isolating the diazo-derived products is what makes the case this is real chemistry and not a one-off. Niche substrate, but genuinely new bond-swapping territory.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Dynamic Dual‐Site Relay Catalysis Enables Selective Solar‐Driven CO 2 Reduction Toward Ethanol
title: Two catalytic sites tag-teaming CO2 straight to ethanol
blurb: A defect-engineered WO3-x/In single-atom photocatalyst splits the labor: oxygen-vacancy tungsten sites keep feeding *CO from CO2, indium single atoms handle the C-C coupling that actually makes ethanol. Solar CO2-to-ethanol usually stalls right at that coupling step, so giving it a dedicated site is the part worth noticing.

original_title: Analytical Quality By Design-Based Development And Validation Of A Stability-Indicating RP-HPLC Method For Simultaneous Determination Of Triamcinolone Acetonide And Econazole Nitrate In Pharmaceutical Cream Formulation
title: Same steroid-antifungal cream assay, run through a Central Composite Design
blurb: A stability-indicating RP-HPLC method that separates and quantifies triamcinolone acetonide and econazole nitrate together in cream formulations, with the chromatographic conditions optimized via AQbD rather than trial and error. Solid QC plumbing, unglamorous by design.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Understanding the Ultrafast Crystallization Kinetics of Donor–Acceptor Semiconducting Polymers
title: Polymer semiconductors crystallize before you can blink, so they built a calorimeter fast enough to watch
blurb: Donor-acceptor semiconducting polymers like PTQ10 and D18 crystallize in under a second at 300°C+, too fast for the usual step-by-step calorimetry to catch honestly. A single-step fast scanning calorimetry setup gets real isothermal kinetic data down to tenths of a second instead of stitching it together indirectly.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Role of Lewis centres on ethanol dehydrogenation over the Cu‐Cr/ γ ‐Al 2 O 3 system
title: Ethanol dehydrogenation catalyst that cokes itself to death
blurb: Cu-Cr on gamma-alumina dehydrogenates ethanol better because the Cu-Cr interaction pumps up Lewis acid site density. The catch: soft coke builds up fast on exactly those copper and Cu-Cr sites, killing dehydrogenation activity and handing the reaction over to the alumina's acid sites, which just dehydrate ethanol to ether and ethylene instead.
venue: The Canadian Journal of Chemical Engineering

original_title: Gold-Catalyzed "Anti-Baldwin" Cyclization of Unactivated Alkenes
title: Baldwin's rules broken by letting the kinetic product cyclize back out
blurb: 5-endo-trig cyclizations are supposed to be geometrically disfavored, so most anti-Baldwin examples lean on activated alkenes to force it. Here gold catalysis does it with plain unactivated alkenes by making the kinetically favored 4-exo-trig ring reversible, so it re-opens and equilibrates to the thermodynamic 5-endo-trig intermediate before reductive elimination locks it in.

original_title: Development and Scale-Up of a Regioselective Functionalization of 2-Cyano-3-fluoropyridine in a Flow Reactor
title: Pyridyllithium chemistry that doesn't need a cryostat, in flow
blurb: LDA deprotonation of 2-cyano-3-fluoropyridine usually wants cryogenic temps to keep the pyridyllithium intermediate alive. This flow process does it at -20°C with a 6 second residence time in Corning reactors, then traps it in-line with electrophiles for high-yield, selective functionalization, and scales up cleanly.

original_title: Lutetium-177-PSMA-617 Radiographic PFS Benefit in the PSMAddition Trial for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer - Scott Tagawa - UroToday
title: Lu-177-PSMA-617 shows an rPFS edge in PSMAddition
blurb: Scott Tagawa on the PSMAddition trial: Lu-177-PSMA-617 delivers a radiographic progression-free survival benefit in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.

original_title: Heterocycle‐Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks With Indazole Units for Cooperative H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Biomass Valorization
title: Swapping imine links for indazole ones to make a COF that photosynthesizes H2O2
blurb: These COFs get their indazole linkages from Cadogan reductive cyclization of nitro-imine precursors, trading the usual fragile imine bonds for something sturdier while keeping crystallinity and picking up better visible-light absorption. Paired with furfuryl alcohol oxidation, the two half-reactions apparently help each other: less carrier recombination, more H2O2.

original_title: Base-Mediated Cyclization of N -Benzyl Ketimines with Diynes: Conditions-Controlled Switching between N -Vinyl Pyrroles and 2 H -Azepines
title: Same superbase, same diynes, two different rings depending on conditions
blurb: Azaallyl anions off N-benzyl ketimines meet diaryldiynes in NaOtBu/DMSO and, depending on conditions, do a formal [3+2] to triarylated N-vinyl pyrroles (up to 64%) or a [4+3] to tetraarylated 2H-azepines (up to 75%). Both scale to grams, which is the part that actually makes it useful rather than just cute.

original_title: Stereoelectronically Controlled Regioselective Allylation of Aldehyde Under Photoredox/Chromium Catalysis
title: Steering allylchromium regiochemistry with electronics instead of a directing group
blurb: Getting clean regioselectivity out of α,γ-disubstituted allylmetal intermediates has mostly meant bolting on a coordinating directing group. This one uses a silyl group instead, exploiting α-silyl electronics under photoredox/chromium catalysis to control which end of the allylchromium hits the aldehyde.

original_title: Accelerated Green SN1 Reactions of the 9-Phenyl-9-fluorenyl Group
title: Shaking your way to a greener SN1
blurb: Resonant acoustic mixing speeds up SN1 chemistry on the 9-phenyl-9-fluorenyl group: PhF halides come together fast from PhF-OH in toluene/mineral acid, and RAM of PhF-Br with Et3N in propylene carbonate installs the PhF group on amino ester hydrochlorides, including serine and hydroxyproline, without protecting their alcohol side chains. Saponification by RAM too, so the whole protecting-group installation gets faster and greener.

original_title: Influence of [99mTc]Tc-DTPA extravasation on Gates GFR and the effect of antecubital ROI-based dose correction in renal dynamic scintigraphy.
title: Tc-99m-DTPA leaking out of the vein throws off your GFR number
blurb: Looks at how extravasation of [99mTc]Tc-DTPA skews the Gates GFR estimate in renal dynamic scintigraphy, and whether correcting the injected dose using an antecubital ROI fixes it.
venue: Nucl Med Rev Cent East Eur

original_title: Small‐Crystal SAPO‐34 Preparation by Regulating Precursor Mixing Temperature for Methanol‐to‐Olefins Conversion
title: Smaller SAPO-34 crystals, no new chemistry, just a warmer slurry
blurb: Tuning the mixing temperature of the precursor slurry alone shifts SAPO-34 nucleation and growth mode, giving small crystals without extra templates or steps. Small crystals are what everyone wants for methanol-to-olefins since they resist coking longer, so a one-knob route to get there is worth having.

original_title: Synthesis and Study of Catalytic Activity in Propane Steam Reforming of Ru–Cu and Ru–Ni Alloy Nanoparticles with Compositions in the Miscibility Gap by Thermolysis of the [RuNO(NH3)4OH][M(C2O4)2(H2O)n], M = Cu, Ni
title: Cu and Ni alloyed with Ru straight out of an oxalate salt
blurb: Thermolysis of [RuNO(NH3)4OH][M(C2O4)2(H2O)n] (M = Cu, Ni) gives metastable Ru-Cu and Ru-Ni solid solutions sitting inside their bulk miscibility gap, up to 16 at% Cu or 33 at% Ru, then run on propane steam reforming. The interesting part is making alloys that shouldn't exist at equilibrium, not that they beat some benchmark catalyst.

original_title: Experimental and DFT insights into phase-dependent performance of NiIn1-xSnx (x=0.5 and 0.8) intermetallic catalysts for acetylene hydrogenation
title: Swap Sn into NiIn and you're really just picking a different crystal face
blurb: Two NiIn1-xSnx intermetallics (x = 0.5 and 0.8) expose different facets depending on Sn content, and DFT plus experiment tie that facet switch directly to acetylene hydrogenation selectivity. Composition here is basically a proxy for which face you're stuck with.

original_title: Solid‐Phase Engineered Metal‐Free Carbonized Polymer Dots With Auto‐Generated Rigid Amorphous Network Enabled High‐Temperature Liquid‐Phase Phosphorescence
title: Carbon dots that keep phosphorescing in hot liquid, no metal needed
blurb: A solid-phase route builds metal-free carbonized polymer dots from a single precursor with a rigid amorphous network baked in, giving phosphorescence tunable from 472 to 545 nm and lifetimes up to 65 ms that survive heat and moisture. Organic phosphors usually die the moment they get wet or warm, so the stability claim is the actual news, not the color range.

original_title: Controlled Electrosynthesisof Metal–OrganicFrameworks
title: A field guide to growing MOFs with electricity instead of heat
blurb: A perspective on MOF electrosynthesis, where anodic dissolution and controlled metal-ion release decouple nucleation from growth and let you dial in crystallinity, phase, orientation, and thickness at room temperature. Mechanism roundup, not a new result, aimed at anyone trying to grow MOF films instead of powders.
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters

original_title: Mechanistic Diversity in Photoexcited Radical Redox Chemistry: A Critical Evaluation
title: The photoredox reactions hitting absurd potentials might not work the way people say
blurb: A critical look at photoexcited radical redox, exciting an already-oxidized or -reduced photocatalyst radical to reach potentials ordinary photoredox can't touch. The reactions themselves are real and have enabled some genuinely hard transformations, but the mechanisms proposed to explain them have drawn real doubt, and this is a referee call on that fight rather than a resolution.

original_title: Easily Accessible and Highly Active Heterogeneous Nickel Catalyst Supported by Covalent Organic Framework for In Situ Ethylene Polymerization
title: A COF finally gets used to cage a nickel polymerization catalyst
blurb: Post-synthetic modification pins nickel onto a dipyridyl-functionalized covalent organic framework, and the resulting Ni@PY-COF runs ethylene polymerization at up to 10^6 g/mol/h with decent thermal stability. COF-supported late-transition-metal catalysts apparently hadn't been done before, which is more the point than the activity number.

original_title: Potential-Driven Dual Effects of Cations Regulate CO2 Reduction: The Interplay between Kinetic Promotion and Steric Effects
title: Cations at the electrode help and hurt CO2 reduction at the same time
blurb: Atomic-scale imaging of the Ag/H2O interface during CO2 reduction shows interfacial cations reshaping water structure and proton-coupled electron transfer in ways that help, while also crowding the surface in ways that hurt, with the balance shifting as you change the applied potential. A spatially resolved dual-role mechanism instead of the usual "more cations, better" story.

original_title: Killing resistant tumors with a click
title: A click reaction for tumors that shrug off everything else
blurb: The paper uses a click chemistry step to go after tumors that have already become resistant to standard treatment, per this Nature Biotechnology report.

original_title: Steering Structural Reconstruction in CO2 Electroreduction Catalysts
title: CO2 reduction catalysts don't stay put once you turn the power on
blurb: A review of why electrocatalysts restructure once CO2RR is actually running, and how that reconstruction creates, transforms, and kills active sites across different catalyst classes. Framed as leverage for catalyst design, but it's a synthesis of other groups' mechanistic work rather than new data.

original_title: N-Arylation of Inosine and 2’-Deoxyinosine with Diaryliodonium Reagents and Atropisomerism of the Products
title: Arylating inosine at nitrogen, not oxygen
blurb: First arylations of inosine and 2'-deoxyinosine with diaryliodonium salts, and the open question was whether the ambident purine amide would go for oxygen or the ring nitrogen. They pin it down to nitrogen, run on Cu(OAc)2/Cs2CO3 in toluene at 60°C with Cu(I) as the likely catalytic species, and the products come out atropisomeric.

original_title: TMS-Diazomethane-Mediated Thione Dimerization Enables Access to Photoconvertible Diazaxanthilidene Dyes for Live-Cell Imaging
title: A room-temperature route to photoswitchable diazaxanthilidene dyes
blurb: The tetrasubstituted olefin core of diazaxanthilidene dyes has been a pain to build because the dimerization step is so sterically hindered. A TMS-diazomethane-mediated thione dimerization does it at room temperature instead, opening up new methyl-substituted variants, including hindered ones, that still photoconvert and still play nice in live cells.

original_title: Trichlorination by a single cyanobacterial halogenase in the biosynthesis of lebomboamide A
title: One halogenase, three chlorines
blurb: A single cyanobacterial halogenase handles all three chlorination steps in the biosynthesis of lebomboamide A.

original_title: Rational Design of Prussian Blue Analogs Cathodes With “Dual‐Channel” Structure for Wide‐Temperature‐Range Sodium‐Ion Batteries
title: Etching vacancies into Prussian blue cathodes to survive temperature swings
blurb: Sodium-ion battery cathodes usually choke on sluggish kinetics and transition-metal dissolution outside a narrow temperature window. A one-step in-situ etch carves carbon-nitrogen vacancies into a channel-structured Prussian blue analog, and both the DFT and the experiments agree those vacancies grip transition metals harder and speed up sodium diffusion.

original_title: Hydrosilylation of β-Alkyl- and Aryl-Substituted Styrenes with Arylsilanes Utilizing the Bridged Pincer Homodinuclear Lanthanide Metal Catalysis
title: A dinuclear lanthanide catalyst that finally hydrosilylates internal alkenes cleanly
blurb: Hydrosilylating β-alkyl and aryl styrenes with arylsilanes has been stuck on weak catalysts, poor regiocontrol, and side reactions. A bridged-pincer homodinuclear lanthanide complex adds PhSiH3 across these internal alkenes under mild conditions with moderate to high yields and regioselectivity the field hasn't had.

original_title: Uptake Patterns of Peripheral Ganglia on 18F-MFBG PET/CT in Neuroblastoma Patients
title: Mapping normal ganglion uptake on neuroblastoma PET
blurb: A look at how 18F-MFBG PET/CT uptake shows up in peripheral ganglia of neuroblastoma patients, the kind of background signal that needs mapping before a hot spot on the scan can be called disease.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Advanced Electrochemical Strategies for Label-Free Analysis of Single Bio-Nanoparticles
title: Reading single bio-nanoparticles electrochemically, no labels required
blurb: A survey of electrochemical approaches for detecting and characterizing individual bio-nanoparticles without fluorescent or other labels attached first.

original_title: A Sustainable Pathway for CO2 Utilization: Pd(II)-Embedded Diamino-Functionalized Al(III) MOF Catalyst with High CO2 Sorption Affinity Enabling Recyclable Synthesis of Bioactive Quinazolinones under Atmospheric Pressure Conditions
title: A CO2-breathing MOF that builds quinazolinones at atmospheric pressure
blurb: A Pd(II)-doped, diamino-functionalized aluminum MOF that both grabs CO2 (1048 m²/g surface area, 102 cc/g uptake at 1 bar, 0°C) and uses it to assemble quinazolinones without needing pressurized gas. It's also recyclable, which is the part that actually decides whether this beats the usual stoichiometric routes.

original_title: Alkyl Chain Regulated Aggregated State Luminescence in TICT‐Type AIEgens
title: Tuning TICT-AIE luminescence just by changing the alkyl chain
blurb: TICT-type AIEgens shift color with their surroundings thanks to a twistable donor-acceptor core, and here alkyl chain length is the dial used to control that twisting once the molecules are packed into aggregates.

original_title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about an FDA rejection, 340B court battles, and more
title: FDA spikes a Novartis radiopharma rival over manufacturing
blurb: This roundup's lead: the FDA rejected a radiopharmaceutical therapy on manufacturing grounds, the kind of rejection that would've given Novartis an actual competitor. Also in the mix, more 340B court battles.

original_title: Sulfur‐Modulated Covalent Organic Framework Superstructures With Highly Dense and Fully Accessible Protophilic Sites for High‐Performance All‐Organic Proton Batteries
title: A COF that stops trading site density for site access
blurb: Sulfur-modulated COF superstructures self-assemble into flower shapes via H-bonding and pi-pi stacking, packing in dense protophilic sites without burying them, for all-organic proton batteries. That's exactly the density-versus-accessibility tradeoff COF battery materials usually can't escape.

original_title: Upcycling Poly(ethylene terephthalate) Into High‐Efficient Epoxy Toughener: Hyperbranched Oligomer Induced Nano‐Structural Heterogeneities
title: Turning water bottles into epoxy toughener, one pot at a time
blurb: Waste PET gets converted directly into hyperbranched oligomers loaded with terminal hydroxyls and used as an epoxy toughener, skipping the costly purification and decolorization that monomer-focused PET recycling usually needs.

original_title: MOF‐Derived Hollow CoFe@NC Nanocages for Highly Efficient Degradation of Textile Fibers
title: Hollow CoFe nanocages built to eat polyester
blurb: ZIF-67 nanocubes get run through a cyanometalate-assisted transformation and reductive calcination into hollow CoFe alloy nanocages wrapped in N-doped carbon, aimed at breaking down chemically stubborn 100% polyester textile fibers. The CoFe@NC-600 version is the one they're pushing as the efficient degrader.

original_title: Fluorodeoxyglucose PET/Computed Tomography in Multimodality and Theranostic Workflows.
title: FDG PET/CT's place in the theranostic workflow
blurb: A review of where FDG PET/CT sits within multimodality and theranostic imaging workflows. Thin on specifics beyond that.

original_title: Emergent Supermonomer Directs Spatially Separated Triplet Pair Generation in Dynamic Oligomers
title: Solvents playing matchmaker for singlet fission
blurb: Ab initio MD on tetracene trimers shows polar solvents dynamically assembling adjacent chromophores into a transient, partially delocalized "supermonomer" that's otherwise inaccessible, and that's what generates the spatially separated triplet pair singlet fission needs to dodge recombination losses. Simulation only, but it's a real mechanistic answer to something that's been murky.

original_title: Artificial Photosynthetic Hydrogel Microspheres as a Versatile Platform for Programmable CO2 Valorization
title: Hydrogel microspheres doing photosynthesis's job for CO2
blurb: Alginate/carboxymethyl cellulose hydrogel microspheres compartmentalize a COF/Pt/Cr2O3 photocatalyst for in situ hydrogen evolution alongside microbes, going after the usual material-microbe hybrid failure points: energy supply, phototoxicity, and biotic-abiotic compatibility. A platform paper betting that compartmentalization fixes what just mixing components couldn't.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Orthogonal hydrogenation of alkenes enabled by multifunctional phosphine
title: A phosphine that hydrogenates one alkene and leaves the rest alone
blurb: A phosphorus-mediated proton transfer strategy, with diphenylphosphine playing multiple roles in relay, gives regioselective hydrogenation of multi-substituted alkenes under mild conditions, picking out one alkenyl site while others in the same molecule sit untouched. That kind of orthogonality is usually the hard part.

original_title: Anti-CEACAM5 ADC Precemtabart Tocentecan (M9140) in Chinese Participants With Solid Tumors
title: Merck KGaA's CEACAM5 ADC gets its China trial
blurb: Phase 1, active not recruiting: the anti-CEACAM5 ADC M9140 (precemtabart tocentecan) being tested in Chinese patients with solid tumors and colorectal cancer. Early safety and dosing territory, no efficacy readout here.

original_title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Renewable Pyridines via Oxidative Ring Expansion
title: 3-hydroxypyridines from furfurylamine, no metal catalyst required
blurb: Galvanostatic electrochemistry converts renewable furfurylamine into 3-hydroxypyridines and substituted analogues, up to 100 mA/cm2 in an undivided cell with aqueous electrolyte, in good to excellent yields. They've already run it at 100 g scale in both batch and flow, so this one's past the proof-of-concept stage.

original_title: Photoinduced Reductive Elimination from Sulfur Enables a Unique Synthetic Valorization of Sulfonamides
title: Stripping the sulfonyl off sulfonamides with light
blurb: A newly discovered photochemical desulfonylation pulls the sulfonyl group entirely off aromatic sulfonamides, converting a wide range of N-heteroaryl sulfonamides into N-heteroaryl anilines. Most sulfonamide chemistry keeps that sulfonyl group intact, so this opens up chemical space that's normally locked behind it.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Protocol for Colorectal Tumor Spheroid Culture in Tunable Stiffness Alginate-Based Hydrogels and Subsequent Immunohistochemical Analysis.
title: Tunable-stiffness alginate for growing tumor spheroids
blurb: A step-by-step protocol for culturing colorectal tumor spheroids in alginate hydrogels where you dial the stiffness yourself, then running immunohistochemistry on them afterward. A methods paper, not a finding, but useful if you're setting the assay up.

original_title: Separation and Valorization of Chlorine From Tail Gas Streams
title: Recycling the chlorine the chemical industry usually just neutralizes
blurb: Chlorine-laden tail gas streams normally get dumped into caustic soda, burning NaOH and leaving a low-value waste stream. This swaps that for an ion-exchange resin that selectively grabs chlorine out of the gas mix even with oxygen, nitrogen, CO2, and hydrogen present, so the chlorine gets recovered instead of scrubbed away.

original_title: S -Adenosyl- l -homocysteine Hydrolase Side Reactivity Enables Biocatalytic Access to 4′,5′-Dehydro Nucleosides as Nucleoside Drug Precursors
title: An enzyme's side reaction turns into a nucleoside drug shortcut
blurb: SAH hydrolase's day job is cleaving S-adenosylhomocysteine to keep cellular methylation running, but its side reactivity also builds 4',5'-dehydro nucleosides, a precursor several nucleoside drugs need. Biocatalysis riding an enzyme's known promiscuity rather than an engineered one.

original_title: Fast Diffusion-Based Metabolomics Profiling by 3D Pure Shift HSQC-DOSY NMR with COLMARvista
title: Untangling overlapping metabolite peaks by how fast they diffuse
blurb: NMR metabolomics keeps running into metabolites with near-identical chemical shifts that overlap and get confused for each other. This adds a pure-shift 3D HSQC-DOSY experiment that reads out each metabolite's own diffusion coefficient, plus new software, COLMARvista, to automate the processing, so degenerate shifts stop looking like the same compound.

original_title: Coupled Photon Transport and Interfacial Charge Utilization in ACT/g‐PAN for Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
title: CO2 photoreduction tuned at the reactor level, not just the catalyst
blurb: Most photocatalytic CO2 reduction papers optimize the catalyst molecule and stop there. This one instead varies catalyst loading, light wavelength, and the plasmonic photothermal effect on an Ag/Cu-TiO2/g-PAN system, treating photon transport and charge use as a reactor engineering problem rather than a ligand design one.

original_title: Lignin self-photocatalytic depolymerization
title: Lignin depolymerizing itself under light
blurb: A preprint on lignin breaking itself down photocatalytically, no separate catalyst added. Light on detail so far, but skipping the catalyst entirely would be a nice trick if the numbers back it up.

original_title: Synthesis, Aromaticity, and Optical and Redox Properties of Silicon(IV) and Tin(IV) Complexes of meso -Substituted 5-Monoazaporphyrin Derivatives
title: First group-14 metal complexes of monoazaporphyrins
blurb: Six-coordinate silicon(IV) and tin(IV) complexes of triaryl-5-monoazaporphyrins, made by metalating the free base and then swapping axial ligands (F, Cl, OH, OCOPh). They push further with N-phenylation and N-ethynylation to get tetraaryl salts and ethynyl derivatives, and map how all of it shifts aromaticity and optical/redox behavior. Scope-building for now, not an application.

original_title: Small details with large impacts: guidelines for reproducible NaBH4-mediated syntheses of surfactant-free colloidal gold nanoparticles at room temperature
title: The reaction vessel you grabbed might be why your gold nanoparticles don't reproduce
blurb: Surfactant-free gold nanoparticles from just water, HAuCl4, and NaBH4 sound like about the simplest nanoparticle synthesis there is, seconds at room temperature. The paper's point is that people still can't reproduce it reliably, and traces part of that to things like which reaction vessel you use, the kind of parameter nobody thinks to report.

original_title: Unveiling the Structure–Property Correlations of Acid-Stable Cyclic Imide Dioximes for Enhanced V(V) and U(VI) Sequestration
title: Working out what actually makes these acid-stable ligands grab uranium and vanadium
blurb: Phthalimide dioxime and naphthalimide dioxime are acid-stable ligands built for pulling U(VI) and V(V) out of secondary sources, relevant to nuclear fuel and vanadium flow batteries. This works out their real coordination modes and stability constants in methanol/water, tying the aromatic backbone to binding strength rather than just reporting extraction numbers.

original_title: Towards Reactive Electrochemical Transport Using the Lattice Boltzmann Method. Part I: Electrostatics, Hydrodynamics, Species Transport, and Electrokinetic Benchmarking
title: Building a lattice Boltzmann solver for electrochemistry, one benchmark at a time
blurb: Part I of a Fortran lattice Boltzmann framework meant to eventually handle reactive electrochemical transport, but this installment is just the validation: electrostatics, hydrodynamics, ion transport, and electrokinetics checked against analytical benchmarks. No actual reactions yet, just making sure the physics underneath holds before they add them.

original_title: Novel furo[2,3-d]pyrimidinones as direct thrombin inhibitors: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation
title: A new furopyrimidinone scaffold aimed straight at thrombin
blurb: Direct thrombin inhibitors built on a furo[2,3-d]pyrimidinone core, taken through synthesis and biological testing. It's in Bioorganic & Medicinal Chemistry, so read it as an early structure-activity pass rather than anything near the clinic.

original_title: Controlled Self-Assembly of [2]-Catenanes Via Tuning the Length and Conjugation Area of Flexible Building Units
title: Catenane topology, dialed in by linker length
blurb: Rhodium half-sandwich building blocks paired with heteroaryl amide ligands to test how far [2]-catenane self-assembly can be steered by tuning linker length and conjugation area. Pyrazine and thiophene ligands with methylene linkers reliably give D-type catenanes, so in this system the linker really is the thing deciding the topology.

original_title: Double-modified guar gum dual-network hydrogels with balanced mechanical and swelling properties.
title: A guar gum hydrogel that doesn't have to choose between strength and swelling
blurb: Double-modified guar gum forms a dual-network hydrogel that balances mechanical strength against swelling capacity, the usual tradeoff these gels fight. Not much more to go on than that from Int J Biol Macromol.

original_title: Improved Purification of sgRNA and pegRNA by Use of a 5′-Terminal Dioctyloxytrityl (DOT) Protecting Group
title: A trityl cap that makes sgRNA purification less painful
blurb: A 5'-terminal dioctyloxytrityl (DOT) protecting group used to purify sgRNA and pegRNA, pulling full-length product away from the truncated and side-reaction junk that piles up when you synthesize long structured oligos. Aimed at the standard RNA therapeutics headache: impurities that either tank yield or trigger off-target and immune effects.

original_title: Manufacturing problems cited in FDA rejection of ITM's radiopharma drug - Endpoints News
title: ITM's radiopharma drug hits an FDA manufacturing wall
blurb: FDA rejected ITM's radiopharmaceutical over manufacturing problems, not the efficacy or safety data. That's the more fixable flavor of rejection, but it's still a delay nobody on that program wanted.
